source: Chrysikou, Weber & Thompson-Schill (2014) A matched filter hypothesis for cognitive control
finding: Core theory. Prefrontal control is a filter that helps some tasks and hurts others. The best level of control depends on the task. High control suits explicit, rule-based, verbal, abstract tasks that fit working memory. Low control suits implicit, reward-based, non-verbal, intuitive tasks.
numbers: Review and synthesis, no new data. Only the abstract was read this session (Europe PMC).
quote: not an all-purpose optimization system suited to every problem
limits: Review, not a test. Hard to falsify without an independent measure of task type. Full text not opened.
agent_relevance: Basis for O4: relax constraints when the problem is open-ended, keep strict control when it is rule-based. Control level should be a per-task setting, not a fixed one.

source: Chrysikou & Thompson-Schill (2011) Dissociable brain states linked to common and creative object use
finding: First fMRI test of the trade-off. Retrieving a common use of an object (blowing your nose with a tissue) activated lateral prefrontal cortex. Generating a creative use activated occipito-temporal cortex. The anterior to posterior balance flipped with task openness.
numbers: N = 24 participants. Closed task (Common Use) versus open task (Uncommon Use). Activation in middle occipital gyrus tracked the type of response on the open task.
limits: Abstract only read. Small N. Reverse inference from regions to processes. The two tasks differ in more than control demand.
agent_relevance: Supports a mode switch: a closed retrieval step and an open generation step should be different states with different constraint levels.

source: Dietrich (2003) Functional neuroanatomy of altered states of consciousness: the transient hypofrontality hypothesis
finding: Proposes that altered states (dreaming, endurance running, meditation, daydreaming, hypnosis, drugs) share transient prefrontal down-regulation. Lower control frees associative processing. Later extended to creativity (flow, improvisation).
numbers: Theory paper. Evidence is a literature integration, no single effect size.
limits: Abstract only read. Later imaging of divergent thinking and improvisation also shows prefrontal activation (Beaty 2015), which competes with a pure hypofrontality account.
agent_relevance: Gives the strong version of the trade-off: less control may help generation. Treat it as a hypothesis for the generation state only (G1: change mode on a signal).

source: Beaty, Benedek, Silvia & Schacter (2016) Creative Cognition and Brain Network Dynamics (Trends in Cognitive Sciences)
finding: Across divergent thinking, poetry and jazz improvisation, the default and executive networks, which usually oppose each other, tend to cooperate. This is the main challenge to a pure trade-off.
numbers: Review of fMRI studies. No pooled effect size in the abstract.
limits: Abstract only read. Network coupling is correlational and its direction in time is unclear.
agent_relevance: Control and free association may need to run together, with control steering and evaluating. Matches a loop where drafts are evaluated by a program (G2, G3).

source: Beaty, Benedek, Barry Kaufman & Silvia (2015) Default and Executive Network Coupling Supports Creative Idea Production (Sci Rep)
finding: During Alternate Uses versus an object-characteristics control, a distributed network included default hubs (left precuneus, right PCC, bilateral inferior parietal lobule), right DLPFC (executive) and insula/ACC (salience). Network efficiency rose with divergent thinking ability. Early in the task default regions coupled with salience regions, later with executive regions.
numbers: fMRI N = 25 (13 female, age 18-30; 3 of 28 excluded for motion). Resting-state check on an independent sample N = 42. MVPA plus seed-to-voxel plus sliding-window connectivity (p < .05 FWE).
quote: increased coupling between default and executive network regions at later stages
limits: Small sample. Connectivity is not causal. The time-course claim rests on a few windows. Authors argue the usual DMN-ECN antagonism may be an artifact of externally focused paradigms.
agent_relevance: Suggests two phases: start with free, salience-driven generation, then bring in control for evaluation. Fits a schema where checks come after drafting.

source: Beaty et al. (2015) Sci Rep, resting-state check and discussion of when networks cooperate
finding: At rest, PCC and precuneus seeds were negatively connected to DLPFC, and the DLPFC seed was negatively connected to default regions. During divergent thinking the same default and executive hubs became positively coupled. The authors say executive and default networks cooperate when extended evaluation of internal information is needed (future planning, constructive daydreaming, evaluating creative ideas).
numbers: Resting-state sample n = 42. Task coupling seeds: precuneus and PCC with right MFG (BA 9/10) and insula; right DLPFC with right IPL, left PCC and right precuneus.
limits: The artifact claim about external-attention paradigms is an argument, not a direct test.
agent_relevance: Control is not only suppressive. It can point attention inward, which matches an agent that evaluates its own draft against external checks.

source: Benedek, Franz, Heene & Neubauer (2012) Differential effects of cognitive inhibition and intelligence on creativity (Pers Individ Differ)
finding: Inhibition (random motor generation) correlated positively with divergent thinking, mostly fluency and flexibility. Intelligence predicted originality. Intelligence mediated the link from inhibition to originality.
numbers: N = 104 (79 women, mean age 23.6, SD 4.0). Fluency and flexibility r = .86. SEM chi2(145) = 196.59, CFI .90, RMSEA .06. Mediation estimate .23, 95% CI .04-.42 (1000 bootstraps). Paths: inhibition to flexibility .55; intelligence to originality .51; inhibition to intelligence .52.
quote: Cognitive inhibition ... appears to substantially facilitate the fluent generation of new ideas
limits: Students, correlational, one inhibition task. A compound divergent-thinking latent fit badly (RMSEA .15), so fluency and originality were split post hoc. Opposes the disinhibition view.
agent_relevance: Control helps quantity (not getting stuck on earlier answers), general ability helps originality. In an agent, deduplicating against earlier attempts is cheap control; novelty needs something else.

source: Benedek et al. (2012), introduction: three rival views and cited behavioral findings
finding: The paper sets out three positions: creativity needs effective inhibition, creativity is disinhibition (decreased latent inhibition in high creative achievers), or creativity needs adaptive control. It cites that creative people are slower on interference trials but faster on trials without interference, and that fluent new uses were predicted by letter fluency while familiar uses were not.
numbers: Second-hand summary of cited studies. No numbers from the originals were read.
limits: Second-hand through one paper. Originals not opened. Evidence is described by the authors as conflicting.
agent_relevance: Control strength is not monotonic. Test adaptive switching: tighten or loosen constraints on a measured signal, not on a schedule.

source: Zabelina et al. (2018) Creativity and cognitive control: behavioral and ERP evidence that divergent thinking, but not real-life creative achievement, relates to better cognitive control (Neuropsychologia)
finding: Two ERP studies. Divergent thinkers switched attention levels faster on rare targets and showed a larger anterior N2 difference (more control at the switch). Real-life creative achievement showed neither effect.
numbers: Two experiments, oddball task with hierarchical letters. Results held after controlling for intelligence. Sample sizes not read.
limits: Abstract only. Divergent thinking and real achievement dissociate. Not a test of control strength as such.
agent_relevance: Flexible control (switching on demand) matters more than strong control. Supports switching on a signal (G1).

source: Weinberger, Green & Chrysikou (2017) Using Transcranial Direct Current Stimulation to Enhance Creative Cognition: Interactions between Task, Polarity, and Stimulation Site (Front Hum Neurosci)
finding: Cathodal tDCS over left inferior frontotemporal cortex helped idea generation tasks. Anodal tDCS over left DLPFC or frontopolar cortex helped idea selection tasks. Green et al. found anodal left frontopolar stimulation raised semantic distance in analogy matrix search, with a stimulation by creativity-cue interaction in verb generation.
numbers: Review. Effects depend on site, polarity and task. Study Ns not pooled.
quote: Cathodal stimulation over the left inferior frontotemporal cortex has been associated with improvements on tasks that rely primarily on idea generation
limits: Heterogeneous designs, small studies, tDCS spread is imprecise. Recent meta-reviews cited in Rosen 2016 find no working-memory benefit of anodal right DLPFC.
agent_relevance: Generation and selection want opposite control settings. Supports separate states for drafting versus choosing (O4 versus checks).

source: Rosen, Erickson, Kim, Mirman, Hamilton & Kounios (2016) Anodal tDCS to Right Dorsolateral Prefrontal Cortex Facilitates Performance for Novice Jazz Improvisers but Hinders Experts (Front Hum Neurosci)
finding: Anodal tDCS to right DLPFC (1.5 mA, 15 min) had no main effect but interacted with expertise. It helped less experienced pianists and hurt the most experienced. Expertise itself (log gigs) strongly predicted creativity ratings.
numbers: Jazz pianists, gigs M = 108.5 (SD 125.3, range 3-400). Expertise model chi2 = 20.74, p < .001. Expertise x tDCS chi2(4) = 9.84, p = .043. Judge ICC: creativity .81, technical .77, aesthetic .84 (4 judges).
limits: Small sample, almost all male (2 women), p = .043 is marginal, no replication found this session.
agent_relevance: Optimal control depends on skill. Novices need explicit control, experts do better automatically. A strong model on familiar problems may need less scaffold, weak spots more.

source: Rosen et al. (2016) discussion: why novices gain and experts lose
finding: Authors read the result as a dual-process pattern. Explicit top-down control helps novices whose associative knowledge is not yet automatic. They note that if tDCS simply strengthened the network, experts should also improve, which did not happen.
numbers: Same data as above. Working-memory benefits of anodal right DLPFC are not supported by recent meta-reviews (cited in the paper).
limits: Interpretation only. DLPFC holds many functions that tDCS cannot separate.
agent_relevance: A weak solver gains from imposed structure, a strong one can be harmed by it. Match the scaffold to measured skill.

source: Khalil, Karim, Kondinska & Godde (2020) Effects of transcranial direct current stimulation of left and right inferior frontal gyrus on creative divergent thinking are moderated by changes in inhibition control (Brain Struct Funct)
finding: Left-down right-up IFG stimulation changed only Alternate Uses originality compared with the opposite montage. Inhibitory control (Go/NoGo) did not change overall, so mediation by inhibition was not confirmed. A moderation held: gains in originality and flexibility only when inhibitory control also improved.
numbers: Cathodal left plus anodal right N = 19, opposite N = 21. Originality F(1,35) = 5.47, p = .025, partial eta2 = .135. Flexibility trend t(40) = 1.92, p = .062. Fluency: baseline covariate only (F = 9.31, p = .004).
limits: Small groups, p near threshold, no sham group described. Partly a failed test of the inhibition story.
agent_relevance: The control-creativity link may depend on whether control actually shifts. Do not assume that loosening or tightening works without a measure.

source: Zhang, Qiao, Chen, Yang, Xu, Yao, Qiu & Yang (2016) Gray Matter Volume of the Lingual Gyrus Mediates the Relationship between Inhibition Function and Divergent Thinking (Front Psychol)
finding: Inhibition function was linked to divergent thinking fluency and originality through gray matter volume in the lingual gyrus, a posterior region.
numbers: Right lingual gyrus, originality: a = -0.231 (p = .005), b = 0.30 (p = .002), indirect -0.069, 95% CI -0.154 to -0.02. Fluency indirect -0.067. Left lingual: indirect -0.056 (originality), -0.051 (fluency). Controlled for intelligence, gender and age.
limits: Structural, cross-sectional, mediation not causal. Sample size not recorded here.
agent_relevance: Fits an anterior-posterior picture: prefrontal control acts on posterior retrieval regions. Still a correlation.

source: Zhang et al. (2016), introduction: generation as bottom-up and evaluation as top-down
finding: The paper summarizes a two-stage view: generation is bottom-up with diffuse attention, evaluation is top-down with focused attention and cognitive control, and these map to default and control networks. It also notes contradictory findings on inhibition and creativity.
numbers: Narrative summary, no counts.
limits: Authors' framing, not a pooled test.
agent_relevance: Same split as our states: draft loosely, then check strictly (G2).

source: Peeperkorn, Kouwenhoven, Brown & Jordanous (2024) Is temperature the creativity parameter of large language models?
finding: Temperature is a crude analogue of lowering control. Raising it gave only weak gains in novelty and cost coherence. No relation to typicality or cohesion.
numbers: Llama 2-Chat 70B, 7 temperatures from 0.001 to 2.0, 31 stories, 5 per temperature, human raters. Novelty slope .308 (SE .138, Rc2 .385). Coherence slope .240 (SE .122, Rc2 .646; higher means less coherent). Inter-rater alpha .639.
limits: One model, one prompt, non-expert raters, small story set. Sampling noise is not the same thing as reduced executive control.
agent_relevance: Warning for O4: loosening by raising temperature trades coherence for little novelty. Prefer structured relaxation plus a check.

source: Peeperkorn et al. (2024), diversity measures
finding: Higher temperatures did not widen the semantic range of stories much. Outputs at higher temperature overlapped heavily with outputs at lower temperature in embedding space. Temperature mainly raises the chance of finding novelty sooner.
numbers: Cosine similarity to the greedy exemplar story showed only a weak negative trend with temperature. Edit distance changed immediately at 0.334 < t < 1.0, with no clear gain above t = 1.0.
limits: Single prompt and model. Limited samples per temperature.
agent_relevance: Relaxing sampling spreads wording, not ideas. Frame changes (operators) are the likelier source of real novelty.

source: Bellemare-Pepin, Lespinasse, Thoelke, Harel, Mathewson, Olson, Bengio & Jerbi (2024/2025) Divergent Creativity in Humans and Large Language Models
url: not verified; full text read from a downloaded PDF, id unconfirmed
finding: On the Divergent Association Task, GPT-4 beat the average of 100,000 humans and GeminiPro matched humans, but the top models stayed below highly creative humans. GPT-4 improved with temperature.
numbers: GPT-4 mean DAT 85.6 at the highest temperature (1.5 of 0.5/1.0/1.5), above 72% of human scores. GPT-4-turbo scored lower than GPT-4. A later check (June 2025 models) found top-decile, top-quartile and above-median humans still above every listed model.
limits: The DAT measures word distance only. One prompt format. Authors discuss data contamination risk.
agent_relevance: For single-word semantic spread, loosening sampling does help, unlike story coherence. The task decides whether loosening pays (matched filter logic).

source: Bellemare-Pepin et al. (2024/2025), validity check and writing tasks
url: not verified; full text read from a downloaded PDF, id unconfirmed
finding: Every model scored significantly higher on the DAT when given DAT instructions than when asked for a generic list of ten words, confirming compliance. Lower-scoring models were more variable and often failed to follow the instruction. Creative writing was scored with Divergent Semantic Integration.
numbers: Pairwise contrasts all significant except Humans/GeminiPro, GeminiPro/Claude3 and Vicuna/GPT-3.5. Vicuna, a much smaller model, beat some larger ones.
limits: Automated scoring with known limits. Model size did not predict score.
agent_relevance: Measure with a compliance control before trusting a creativity score.

source: Schapiro, Park, Varshney & Sosa (2026) CreativityNeuro: Steering Language Model Weights to Improve Divergent Thinking and Reduce Mode Collapse
finding: Contrastive weight steering with no training data raised divergent thinking and cut mode collapse in six open models (3B to 14B). Activation steering matched it on DAT but did not transfer to the Alternative Uses Test or the Task Task.
numbers: DAT: up to +14 human percentile points. Human evaluation N = 720 on AUT and Task Task, significant gains in originality, surprise and creativity. Models: LLaMA 3.2-3B and 3.1-8B, Qwen2.5 7B and 14B, Phi-3.5-mini and Phi-3-medium.
limits: Preprint. About weight space, not prefrontal control. Not usable in a scaffold-only agent.
agent_relevance: Shows LLMs have a default converge mode that can be moved. Gives a mode-collapse baseline we could test against.

source: Schapiro et al. (2026) CreativityNeuro, mode-collapse measurements
finding: Baseline models put a quarter of their DAT tokens on a few words. CreativityNeuro reduced that share and raised vocabulary entropy. Three words (galaxy, quasar, xylophone) were in the top 30 of all three model families.
numbers: Baseline top-10 word share 25.5% of tokens. CN cut it by 10.2 points and raised entropy by 0.59 nats (+10%). AUT intra-model repetition down 2.4% (CN) versus 6.6% (activation steering); TT down 5.5% versus 3.0%. Inter-model homogeneity AUT 3.3% versus 4.7%, TT 6.3% versus 2.5%.
limits: Single-digit percent homogeneity changes. Temperature settings 0.9, 1.0, 1.2 for DAT.
agent_relevance: Samples from one model are not independent (G4): measurable shared words across families support that.

source: Mondal, Webb & Momennejad (2025) Improving planning with large language models: a modular agentic architecture (MAP; Nature Communications)
finding: Prefrontal-inspired LLM modules (conflict monitor, predictor, evaluator, decomposer, orchestrator) improved planning. The Monitor filtered invalid actions, so no invalid actions in the graph tasks.
numbers: Valuepath 100% solved. Tower of Hanoi 3-disk: nearly seven-fold more problems solved than zero-shot, 100% on best of 5 runs; 4-disk is out of distribution and single run. Beats CoT, multi-agent debate and tree-of-thought.
limits: Tasks are closed and rule-based, where the matched filter view predicts control helps. Not a creativity test.
agent_relevance: A cognitive-control architecture in LLM form: separate code-checked modules. Fits G2 and G3.

source: Mondal et al. (2025), neuroscience basis of the modules
finding: The paper maps modules onto prefrontal subregions: conflict monitoring (ACC), state prediction and evaluation (orbitofrontal), task decomposition (anterior PFC), and orchestration. It cites Miller and Cohen's integrative theory of PFC function and Russin et al. on deep learning needing a prefrontal cortex.
numbers: No new behavioral numbers in this section.
limits: Analogy, not evidence that the modules act as the brain regions do.
agent_relevance: Borrowed design only. Our schema already splits program-level control from model-level generation.

source: Synthesis of the brain-stimulation evidence read this session (Weinberger 2017, Rosen 2016, Khalil 2020)
finding: Stimulation effects on creativity are small, site-specific and conditional. Rosen found no main effect, Khalil found only 1 of 3 divergent-thinking scores moved and the inhibition mediation failed.
numbers: Rosen interaction p = .043. Khalil originality p = .025, flexibility p = .062, N = 40 total.
limits: Our reading of three papers, not a systematic search. No large preregistered replication found.
agent_relevance: Treat the control-creativity trade-off as plausible but fragile (status [S]). Measure before building rules on it.

source: Rosen et al. (2016) Front Hum Neurosci, rating scales
finding: Judges' ratings of creativity, aesthetic appeal and technical proficiency were almost the same thing. Expertise predicted ratings better than age, music training years or jazz training years.
numbers: Creativity-aesthetic r(100) = .96; creativity-technical r(100) = .91; aesthetic-technical r(100) = .93 (all p < .01). Model fit: expertise chi2 = 20.74 vs age 3.49, music training 2.65, jazz training 2.71.
limits: Rated quality may mix creativity with polish, so the tDCS-by-expertise result may be about overall quality.
agent_relevance: A creativity score that tracks general quality cannot separate novelty from competence. Score novelty separately.
